subject: Marketplace SKU & packaging — multi-cloud rollout plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com; jane@cloudsphere.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace SKU & packaging — initial options

Team / Jane,

Following up from yesterday’s partner sync — I’ve sketched three candidate approaches for how we list Redwood on each cloud marketplace and what to prioritize for co-sell enablement. High level: keep the offerings consistent from a buyer perspective, but use cloud-specific packaging where it enables co-sell or simplified procurement.

Options (short):
- Option A (SaaS transactable on marketplaces): Host in our hosted mode, transactable offers on AWS/Azure/GCP, metered billing. Pros: easiest for customers to buy, co-sell benefits. Cons: more compliance/integration work per cloud.
- Option B (Private/Bring-Your-Own-Infra SKUs): Images/managed app that customers deploy in their cloud or VPC. Pros: faster to list in some GTM programs, simpler for regulated customers. Cons: weaker co-sell/marketplace conversion.
- Option C (Hybrid SKUs): Lightweight SaaS listing for trial & small customers + BYOL/Private SKU for enterprise/procurement. Pros: covers both motions but requires SKU mapping and regional parity work.

Key questions I want input on:
1) Which clouds do we invest in transactable SaaS offers first? (AWS/Azure/GCP)
2) Which regions should be guaranteed at launch for each cloud (must-have vs later)?
3) Metering strategy: per-token vs vCPU-hour vs seat?
4) Packaging: single SKU with tiered rails or separate SKUs per capacity/throughput?

I’ve attached a first-pass SKU matrix for AWS (rafael — I asked you to fill), an Azure checklist, and the GCP co-sell doc. Please reply with redlines or vote on A/B/C by Thu EOD. Jane, any constraints from CloudSphere on co-sell eligibility/timing?

Thanks — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: aws_sku_matrix_v1.csv] [Attachment: azure_offer_checklist.pdf] [Attachment: gcp_co_sell_requirements.docx]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: jane@cloudsphere.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU & packaging — initial options

+1 on Option C (hybrid). I filled the AWS matrix with suggested SKUs and naming conventions — see aws_sku_matrix_v1.csv attached. Notes:
- AWS: recommend two transactable SaaS SKUs at launch (standard / enterprise) which meter by monthly aggregated tokens (token tiers: 0-10M, 10M-100M, 100M+). Helps simplify billing reconciliation for customers.
- For high-performance instances we offer an "accelerator" SKU (reserved capacity) priced per vGPU-hour and surfaced as an add-on.
- Regions to prioritize: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1. For the first phase, skip ap-east and southamerica until we have concise demand signals.

Open items:
1) Are we comfortable exposing token-metering in marketplace usage reports, or do we push invoicing to our billing system and use marketplace for initial payment only?
2) We need legal to confirm refund rules for metered SaaS on AWS.

Attaching the matrix.

--
Rafael Mendes
Director, Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: aws_sku_matrix_v1.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, jane@cloudsphere.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU & packaging — initial options

Nice work. Azure specifics:
- Co-sell on Azure requires a managed application or transactable SaaS offer with publisher validation. The co-sell share/visibility is significant if we meet their program checklist (see attached checklist).
- Azure marketplace handles metered billing but their meter dimensions are more prescriptive; seat or unit-based meters are easier to align to. Token-based meters are supported but will add engineering overhead to report usage via ARM APIs.
- Recommendation: For Azure, launch with a tiered SKU (Bronze/Silver/Gold) that maps to tokens behind the scenes but is presented as capacity tiers for the buyer. This avoids exposing token accounting in the UI.

Regions: eu-west-1 is not an Azure region name — we should map cloud-region parity carefully. Start with East US, West Europe, and Southeast Asia (if we want APAC presence on Azure early).

Questions:
- Lauren, do we have bandwidth to implement ARM usage reports for month 1? If not, we should delay Azure transactable and instead do a private/managed offer to get co-sell conversations started.

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: azure_offer_checklist.pdf]

From: Jane Kim <jane@cloudsphere.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU & packaging — initial options

Vanessa / team — thanks for pulling this together. A few things from CloudSphere partner ops and our buyer feedback: 
- AWS ISV Accelerate: strong preference that the SaaS offer is transactable and has clear usage reporting; AWS teams push buyers to marketplace-first purchases.
- Azure co-sell: our joint GTM with Azure expects a transactable marketplace offer within 60 days to qualify for their co-sell motions. If you cannot complete ARM metering in that window, consider the managed app route as a short-term bridge.
- GCP: more flexibility; they value partner GTM motion and references. GCP sells prefer a monthly subscription SKU over complicated metering unless the buyer is metering-native.

Procurement note from our buyer footprint: they want region parity for EU + US at launch for enterprise deals. Non-critical regions can be deferred.

Timeline ask: if Redwood can commit to an AWS + Azure transactable offer (US + EU regions) within 60 days, CloudSphere will prioritize our joint co-sell introductions to two named prospects.

Thanks — Jane

--
Jane Kim
Strategic Partnerships, CloudSphere
jane@cloudsphere.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: jane@cloudsphere.com
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 10:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU & packaging — initial options

Summary and decisions (votes + rationale):
- Decision: pursue Option C (Hybrid) with prioritized transactable offers on AWS and Azure first, GCP transactable in phase 2.
- Regions at launch: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1); Azure (East US, West Europe); GCP (deferred to phase 2)
- Metering: present capacity tiers in marketplace UI (Bronze/Silver/Gold) mapped internally to token buckets. For AWS we will expose token-metering reports to reconcile usage; for Azure we will present tiers and implement ARM reporting if dev bandwidth allows within 60 days.
- SKU naming: Redwood Standard (Bronze), Redwood Pro (Silver), Redwood Enterprise (Gold) + optional 'Accelerator' add-on for reserved GPU capacity.

Owner assignments / next steps:
- Rafael: finalize AWS SKU matrix and coordinate with Finance/legal on refund rules (due 3/20). [attachment: marketplace_pricing_model_v3.xlsx]
- Marcus: confirm Azure ARM usage feasibility and estimate dev effort (ticket to be created) by 3/18.
- Lauren: open engineering epic for region parity and packaging automation; create initial tickets for marketplace CI/CD (due 3/19).
- Vanessa: draft co-sell one-pager for CloudSphere and Azure/AWS partner reps (due 3/17).

Jane — appreciate the timing note. If CloudSphere can commit intros after we publish AWS + Azure transactable offers, we will push to meet the 60-day ask.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: marketplace_pricing_model_v3.xlsx]
